PETER PREVOT, AN ENEMY OF THE CHINESE PEOPLE

Peter Prevot, a British subject, was arrested by
the Chinese authorities in Hankow on July 5 on suspicion of
being a spy. It has now been definitely ascertained that
he was a spy in the employ of the Japanese. His activities
will not affect the diplomatic relations between China and
Great Britain. Peter Prevot is now an enemy of the Chinese
people.

There is no doubt that Peter Prevot's object in
working as a spy for the Japanese was to make money. It
should not be overlooked that China is now carrying on a
war of resistance not only for the sake of her own existence
and the peace of the Far East but for the assurance of
international peace as well. The authorities of the
foreign Powers in China should impress this upon the minds
of their nationals. They should check the movements of
their nationals and assist China by removing such persons
from the employ of Japanese.

彼得·普雷沃，中国人民的敌人

英籍人士彼得·普雷沃（Peter Prevot）于7月5日在汉口被中国当局以涉嫌间谍活动为由逮捕。现已确切查明，他是受雇于日本人的间谍。他的活动不会影响中英两国的外交关系。彼得·普雷沃现在是中国人民的敌人。

毫无疑问，彼得·普雷沃为日本人充当间谍的目的是为了赚钱。不应忽视的是，中国目前进行的抗战不仅是为了自身的生存和远东的和平，也是为了确保国际和平。在华各外国列强的当局应向其国民强调这一点。他们应管束其国民的行动，并通过使此类人员脱离日本人的雇佣来协助中国。

Spy Suspect
Pleads Guilty
In Hankow

Prevot Accepts Charges
But Denies Harboring
Anti-Chinese Motive

HANKOW, July 20.—(Reuters).—
The case against Mr. Peter Prevot,
British subject who was last month
detained by the Chinese authorities
for alleged espionage activities, was
heard in the British Consular Court
here this morning.
Mr. Prevot, who was born in
Hongkong, was detained in Wu-
chang on June 28 while boarding
a plane for Hongkong.
On hearing of Mr. Prevot's ar-
rest, Mr. C. E. Whitamore, British
Consul-General in Hankow, request-
ed that he be handed over to him,
and this request was immediately
complied with.

Pleaded Guilty
Mr. Prevot pleaded guilty at this
morning's hearing to infringement
of Article 89 of the China Order-
in-Council of 1925, which states:—
"Where it is proved that there
is reasonable ground to apprehend
that the acts or conduct of a Bri-
tish subject are likely to produce
or excite a breach of public peace,
the Court may require him to give
security to keep the peace or for
his future good behavior."
In pleading guilty to the charge,
Mr. Prevot's counsel, Mr. C. E.
Sherwin, said that the defendant
wished to state that while his
methods of gathering information
might well cause the Chinese to
become suspicious, he did not in-
tend to use such information to the
detriment of China.
The Court ordered Mr. Prevot to
furnish security of $5,000 on two
sureties, both British subjects re-
sident in Hankow.

普雷沃接受指控

汉口，7月20日.—（路透社）.—
针对英籍人士彼得·普雷沃先生一案于今晨在此地的英国领事法庭开庭审理。普雷沃先生上月因涉嫌从事间谍活动而被中国当局拘留。
普雷沃先生出生于香港，于6月28日在武昌登机前往香港时被拘留。
获悉普雷沃先生被捕后，英国驻汉口总领事 C. E. Whitamore 先生要求将其移交给他，该请求立即得到照办。

认罪
在今晨的庭审中，普雷沃先生对违反1925年《中国枢密院令》第89条的行为表示认罪，该条款规定：—
“如有合理理由担心某英籍人士的作为或行为可能引起或煽动破坏公共和平，法庭可要求其提供担保以保持和平或保证日后行为端正。”
在对指控认罪时，普雷沃先生的辩护律师 C. E. Sherwin 先生表示，被告希望声明，虽然其收集信息的方法很可能引起中国人的怀疑，但他无意利用此类信息损害中国利益。
法庭命令普雷沃先生提供5,000美元保证金，并由两名均居住于汉口的英籍人士作为担保人。

formation to the detriment of

S.V.C.'s Position

To the Editor of the
"NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS"

SIR,—I am surprised that no one
took PREPARED to task for his letter to
you in last Thursday's issue. Refer-
ring to the mill riots and the neces-
sity for maintaining the S.V.C. in
its present form he propounds the
following:

If one small section of the indus-
trial community can cause so much
bother what would the position be if
the trouble was general.

The answer is perfectly simple—
not ten times the present strength of
the S.V.C. would be sufficient to quell
such a disturbance. By the way, was
the rioting element entirely to blame?
Why does PREPARED not enlighten your
readers? He condemns force on one
side and then calmly proceeds to
allow it on the other!

He stands for the maintenance of
the Corps as it is—i.e., as an ex-
tremely expensive military unit with
trappings and paraphernalia that have
nothing in common with the internal
protection of the Settlement. Well
and good. His opinion is entitled to
consideration. But when he wilfully
distorts the contents of the article on
the S.V.C. by an anonymous contri-
butor (in last Wednesday's issue), it
were time indeed that it be pointed
out to him that your readers, whatever
their opinions, stand for fair play.

Times have changed and cir-
cumstances are not what they were.
We one and all have the fullest ad-
miration for the S.V.C. because of
past services, but I feel certain
that every reasonable man, in
the Corps or out, does not
wish to perpetuate a system
which is entirely out-of-date and
which is compelling expenditure that
can be put to much better use.
Sentiment should indeed have its
place were there not other consider-
ations of far greater importance. To
appeal to national bias in order that
a body of men of no military value
should continue to exist is to employ
the usual claptrap of those who pre-
fer the rule of hatred and fear to
that of international friendship and
confidence. No attempt to make of
this matter a political issue should
be tolerated. There is already far
too much of this playing at politics
here and it bodes no good for this
city's future.

Let us protect ourselves against
mob violence (which could be avoid-
ed if we always and at all times
had social justice) by all means. Let
us have a Corps which is purely a
volunteer affair for internal defence
devoid of all unnecessary military
"trimmings," and theatricals; com-
manded by volunteers and run on
the lines of the Police Specials. To
argue that a soldier is better than
a policeman is so ridiculous as to
be worth the mention in order that
the argument be refuted. The dif-
ference lies not in the human element
but in the laws under which each
organization operates. Purely military
affairs should be left in the hands of
the sovereign states interested in
Shanghai. It is their protection and
their protection alone which guar-
antees the Settlement against any
sudden and untoward changes.

P. H. PRIOR.

上海义勇队的地位

致《字林西报》编辑先生：

先生，——我惊讶于竟无人在上周四贵报刊登的来信中，对署名“PREPARED”的作者提出责难。该信谈及纱厂骚乱以及维持上海义勇队（S.V.C.）现有体制的必要性，并提出了如下观点：

如果工业界中一小部分人就能造成如此多的麻烦，那么倘若骚乱普遍发生，局势又将如何？

答案极其简单——即便将上海义勇队目前的兵力增加十倍，也不足以平息此类骚乱。顺便问一下，骚乱分子是否应负全部责任？为何“PREPARED”不向读者阐明这一点？他谴责一方使用武力，却冷静地允许另一方使用武力！

他主张维持义勇队的现状——即作为一个极其昂贵的军事单位，拥有与租界内部防护毫无关系的装饰和附属品。好吧，他的意见值得考虑。但是，当他故意歪曲上周三贵报上一位匿名投稿人关于义勇队文章的内容时，确实应该向他指出，无论持何种观点，贵报读者都主张公平行事。

时代已经改变，情况已非往昔。我们大家都因上海义勇队过去的服务而对其充满敬意，但我确信，无论是队内还是队外的每一位理智人士，都不希望延续一个完全过时、且迫使人们支出本可用于更有益处的资金的制度。如果没有其他更为重要的考量因素，情感确实应有其地位。为了让人一群毫无军事价值的人继续存在而诉诸民族偏见，这是那些宁愿依靠仇恨和恐惧统治、而不愿依靠国际友谊和信任的人所惯用的陈词滥调。不应容忍任何试图将此问题政治化的做法。此地这种政治游戏已经太多，这对这座城市的未来并非吉兆。

让我们务必保护自己免受暴民暴力之害（如果我们始终秉持社会正义，这种暴力本可避免）。让我们建立一支纯粹由志愿者组成、用于内部防御的队伍，摒弃所有不必要的军事“装饰”和作秀；由志愿者指挥，并按照警察特别辅警（Police Specials）的模式运作。声称士兵优于警察的观点荒谬至极，甚至不值一提，除非是为了驳斥它。两者的区别不在于人员素质，而在于各组织运作所依据的法律。纯军事事务应留给关注上海的各个主权国家处理。正是且唯有他们的保护，才能保障租界免受任何突发和不测变故的影响。

P. H. PRIOR.
上海，11月24日。

W L
S R

Subject Peter Henry PREVOT, British.

Made by D.S. Pitts Forwarded by

Peter Henry Prevot, a British subject of French origin,
was born at Victoria, Hongkong on February 1, 1894. He is
in possession of British Passport No.8417 issued in Shanghai
on October 29, 1931.

He has resided in Shanghai for at least twenty years
and is at present living at Apartment No.1, 6th Floor, St.
Anne's Building, 25-41 Rue du Consulat. He also has an office
on the fourth floor of the same building, where he conducts a
stockbroker's business. In addition Prevot acts as resident
engineer and custodian of these apartments, the proprietors
being the French Catholic Fathers, for whom he manages several
other local properties.

A bachelor and an excellent linguist, Prevot was formerly
a member of the majority of the better class Shanghai clubs,
but now retains membership in only a few of them. He has
been a member of the Stock Exchange for several years and
during the boom period in rubber was making as much as $20,000
per month. When the slump set in, however, Prevot went down
heavily, and coupled with the prevalent depression in the
business world, has lost so much that he is now in comparative
straitened circumstances.

Since April, 1936 many articles have appeared in the
columns of the "North China Daily News" signed by Prevot. In
each article or letter, Prevot's object was to bring before the
ratepayers of the Settlement the absolute and urgent necessity
of effecting economy in the conducting of the Municipal Council's
affairs.

Enquiries have indicated that Mr. Prevot has been acting
entirely independently and not on behalf of a group or clique.

彼得·亨利·普雷沃，法裔英籍人士，1894年2月1日出生于香港维多利亚。他持有1931年10月29日在上海签发的第8417号英国护照。

他在上海居住至少已有二十年，目前居住在领事馆路（Rue du Consulat）25-41号圣安妮大楼（St. Anne's Building）六楼1号公寓。他在同一栋大楼的四楼还有一间办公室，从事股票经纪业务。此外，普雷沃还担任这些公寓的驻场工程师和管理人，业主为法国天主教神父，他还为他们管理着当地的其他几处房产。

普雷沃是单身汉，精通语言，曾是上海多数高档俱乐部的会员，但现在仅保留少数几个俱乐部的会籍。他成为证券交易所会员已有数年，在橡胶繁荣时期，月收入高达20,000美元。然而，随着萧条期的到来，普雷沃遭受重创，加上商界普遍的低迷状况，他损失惨重，目前境况相当拮据。

自1936年4月以来，《字林西报》专栏刊登了许多署名为普雷沃的文章。在每篇文章或信件中，普雷沃的目的都是向租界纳税人强调，在工部局事务管理中实行节约具有绝对且紧迫的必要性。

调查显示，普雷沃先生完全是独立行动，并非代表某个团体或小圈子。

Mr. Prevot Replies
To the Editor of the
"NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS"
SIR,—It is surprising what can come from the pen of Mr. H. A. Reeks. That he, a rate-payer of the Settlement, a British Barrister, whose articles have so often appeared in various journals, should presume to impute to me accusations that I have never made and moreover declare as fact something of which he is entirely ignorant, is so unjust that those who have read all my correspondence and can therefore judge me fairly will resent. Apart from which I think his choice of language is somewhat unhappy.
He is intrigued to know for whom I speak. I am just as intrigued to know for whom he speaks. To charge me with rating the members of the S.M.C., with many of whom I am acquainted, as self-seekers, is ridiculous and I choose to ignore the charge. I respect each and every individual who sits on the Council. But I still see no reason for getting sentimental, like J.H.R. did, over their work. I do not believe they seek gratitude. Some may be on the Council because of their public spiritedness, others because they were nominated to represent definite local interests; but as a governing body I, at least, feel that they are not altogether as representative as they might be and from that springs the feeling that our Administration is a select coterie that panders only to certain interests. Right or wrong, this is what is being noised abroad and there can be no harm done in stating it openly. The S.M.C. cannot lay claim to perfection and as a public body its actions are open to criticism. But there has been no attempt in my letters at lowering its prestige nor its powers nor has any attack been delivered at the character of any individual or individuals.
If Mr. Reeks wishes to belittle any efforts I am making to secure for Shanghai what I consider a more representative government and a greater recognition of the rights of the small man, he is at liberty to do so. My person and my ideas or opinions are two very different things. It can hardly matter therefore whether I am a Hottentot or a Bushman. As it happens I do belong to one of the three nationalities that Mr. Reeks names. On that matter of fact therefore he is hopelessly wrong. I have my place of business in the International Settlement and indirectly contribute to its governance and upkeep. And as a citizen of this great city I will continue to maintain the right each of us possesses to freedom of speech.
When speaking of the S.M.C. it is not possible to treat the present one as a separate entity from any of those which preceded it. It is not a Being so much as a form of Government, with very definite policies arrived at after due deliberation. These policies may or may not suit the public. Individual Councillors may change yearly but the Council as a body "goes marching on." This point clearly understood—and anyone with an open mind cannot fail to understand—the cause for criticism of to-day's Council is more readily understood.
Whether the higher ranks in the Councils' employ are overpaid or not is a distinct matter of opinion. I still feel that they are because if it is found necessary to dismiss lowly paid employees and take away from them what is a bare living, those higher up are always in an infinitely better position to take a "cut." This doctrine is somewhat socialistic I admit but it is not for that reason inhuman. It is the whole motif of my correspondence present and past.
As to emoluments in commercial life I have nothing to say, the matter being purely private in nature. Yet, it will be readily admitted that those in commercial undertakings have to accept risks which I do not think are present in a Municipal Service.
I will not enter into a controversy over whether an "orgy of spending" or "economy" is the better way in which to blast Shanghai out of the depression. Here again Mr. Reeks is drawing a red herring across the trail and I do not propose to follow the scent, not liking herrings. Each of these schools of thought on economics has a distinguished following and none has so far been proved correct. Also the real wealth of Shanghai does not come from the presence of a few highly-paid foreigners but from the financial well-being of the masses—the small men.
Dealing more particularly with Shanghai's finances it is evident that the S.M.C. cannot maintain the present rate of expenditure as against income and for that reason it is incumbent upon it to reduce its expenses. (It would be interesting indeed to see such a reducing process being put into application through greater spending!!) I have simply given my ideas as to where reductions may be effected and have done so quite frankly. In the process I was prepared to accept opposition but of the right order. I think opponents like J.H.R. and Mr. Reeks and others would gain by a lesser betrayal of impatience in their public utterances. "Nincompoops," "self-seekers," "envious ones," "carping critics," "snipers," etc. are all names that do nothing more than confirm a weak defence and envenom a discussion which is after all academical.
I have admitted in my correspondence the excellent work done by the S.M.C. and have deprecated the raking up of the "mud" of the past. What has motivated all my criticism has always been clear—those on the lower rungs of the economic or social ladder should not be made to suffer at the expense of those higher up. I speak for no group or groups and have no contacts with any. That explains why my writings have much of the "personal" touch.
It is a great pity that in his concluding paragraph Mr. Reeks admits a tendency to violence of language and vulgarity. If the dignity of the S.M.C. might not be enhanced by the presence of Mr. Reeks (i.e. of course if Mr. Reeks refrains from being violent or vulgar) or myself on that body I for my part cannot see that it would necessarily be diminished. A man's value to a community lies not in his social or economical position but in what is within him and in his desire to serve each and everyone without reference to race, creed, social or economical standing.
I shall always defend any personal charges against me but see no necessity for continuing a discussion in which I have made my stand quite clear. I would like to conclude on one note however—a plea for a better understanding between the various communities in this city. All is not well—at least that is what is generally felt. But cannot sectional misunderstandings be smoothed over to the advantages of all parties?
If asking for consideration to all concerned especially the small men if adherence to my right to criticize the actions of a public body; if pleading for International good-fellowship in an International Settlement is impertinence, then I must choose to remain impertinent.
P. H. PREVOT.
Shanghai, Nov. 3.
（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL COUNCIL - 9 NOV. 1936）

普雷沃先生回复
致《字林西报》编辑

先生，——H. A. 里克斯（Reeks）先生笔下能写出这样的东西，着实令人惊讶。身为租界纳税人、英国出庭律师，且其文章经常见诸各类报刊的他，竟妄加指责我提出过从未提出的指控，更将他全然无知之事宣称为事实，此种不公，令那些读过我所有来信并能对我做出公正评判的人感到愤慨。此外，我认为他的措辞也颇为不当。

他很好奇我代表谁发言。我也同样好奇他代表谁发言。指责我将工部局（S.M.C.）成员——其中许多人与我相识——评为自私自利之徒，这简直荒谬，我选择无视这一指控。我尊重坐在委员会里的每一位个人。但我仍然看不出有任何理由像 J.H.R. 那样对他们的工作感伤起来。我不相信他们在寻求感激。有些人进入委员会是因为他们的公共精神，另一些人则是因为被提名以代表特定的地方利益；但作为一个治理机构，我至少觉得他们的代表性并不如原本可能达到的那样充分，由此产生了一种感觉，即我们的行政当局是一个只迎合某些利益的小圈子。无论对错，这正是外界流传的说法，公开陈述此事并无害处。工部局不能声称完美无缺，作为一个公共机构，其行为应受批评。但在我的信件中，从未试图降低其威望或权力，也未对任何个人或群体的品格发起攻击。

如果里克斯先生希望贬低我为上海争取我认为更具代表性的政府以及更多承认小人物权利所做的任何努力，他尽可如此。我本人与我的思想或观点是两回事。因此，我是霍屯督人（Hottentot）还是布须曼人（Bushman）几乎无关紧要。碰巧我确实属于里克斯先生提到的三个国籍之一。因此，在这一事实问题上，他错得离谱。我在国际租界拥有营业场所，并间接为其治理和维护做出贡献。作为这座伟大城市的公民，我将继续维护我们每个人拥有的言论自由权。

在谈论工部局时，不可能将当前的工部局与之前的任何一个视为独立的实体。它与其说是一个存在体，不如说是一种政府形式，其政策是经过适当审议后确定的。这些政策可能适合公众，也可能不适合。个别董事每年可能会更换，但委员会作为一个整体“继续前行”。这一点一旦清楚理解——任何心态开放的人都不难理解——就更容易理解对当前委员会的批评原因。

委员会雇员中的高层是否薪水过高，这是一个见仁见智的问题。我仍然认为他们薪水过高，因为如果发现有必要解雇低薪员工并夺去他们仅够糊口的收入，那么身居高位者总是处于更有利的地位来承受“减薪”。我承认这种观点有些社会主义色彩，但这并非不人道。这是我过去和现在所有信件的全部主题。

至于商业生活中的薪酬，我无可奉告，因为这纯属私人性质。然而，人们很容易承认，从事商业活动的人必须承担风险，而我认为市政服务中并不存在此类风险。

我不会卷入关于“挥霍开支”还是“节约”哪种方式更能使上海摆脱萧条的争论。在此，里克斯先生再次转移视线（drawing a red herring），我不打算追随这股气味，因为我不喜欢鲱鱼。经济学上的这些思想流派各有众多杰出追随者，迄今尚无一种被证明是正确的。此外，上海真正的财富并非来自少数高薪外国人的存在，而是来自大众——小人物——的经济福祉。

具体谈到上海的财政，显然工部局无法维持目前的支出相对于收入的比率，因此它有责任减少开支。（如果能通过增加支出来实现这种削减过程，那倒是有趣得很！！）我只是坦率地提出了我对可以在何处进行削减的看法。在此过程中，我准备接受反对意见，但必须是合理的反对意见。我认为像 J.H.R.、里克斯先生及其他反对者，如果在公开言论中能少流露一些不耐烦，将会受益。“笨蛋”、“自私自利者”、“嫉妒者”、“吹毛求疵的批评家”、“狙击手”等称呼，除了证实辩护无力并使这场毕竟属于学术性质的讨论变得恶毒之外，别无他用。

我在来信中已承认工部局所做的出色工作，并反对翻出过去的“污泥”。我所有批评的动机始终明确——不应让经济或社会阶梯底层的人以牺牲上层人士为代价而受苦。我不代表任何群体，与任何群体也没有联系。这就解释了我的文章为何带有浓厚的“个人”色彩。

遗憾的是，里克斯先生在结尾段落中承认自己有使用暴力语言和粗俗用语的倾向。如果工部局的尊严不会因里克斯先生（当然，前提是里克斯先生避免暴力和粗俗）或我本人加入该机构而得到提升，那么在我看来，这也不一定会使其尊严受损。一个人对社区的价值不在于其社会或经济地位，而在于其内在品质以及不分种族、信仰、社会或经济地位为每个人服务的愿望。

我将始终捍卫针对我个人的任何指控，但认为没有必要继续一场我已明确立场的讨论。不过，我想以一个呼吁结束本文——呼吁本市各社区之间更好地相互理解。现状并非一切安好——至少这是普遍的感受。但是，难道不能消除派系间的误解，从而使各方受益吗？

如果要求考虑到所有相关方，特别是小人物，坚持我批评公共机构行为的权利；如果在国际租界呼吁国际友好关系被视为无礼，那么我选择保持无礼。

P. H. 普雷沃（PREVOT）
上海，11月3日。

Inquiry Supported
To the Editor of the
"NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS"
SIR,—There is much to be said for your contributor's article in your issue of June 3, anent S.M.C. salaries etc. as he practically advocates what I did, a revision to meet changed conditions. Such revision can best be met by the establishment of a thoroughly independent Commission, composed of men unconnected in any way with the Council and not necessarily business men at that. And I stress the word independent.
Your contributor deprecates blind criticism and suggests that aspersions have been cast upon Municipal servants who cannot by the rules of the game retaliate. I deny that any aspersions whatever have been cast upon individuals holding municipal posts and challenge the writer to prove his statement. Why does he consider the critics any blinder than he? What quality or attribute does he possess which makes him see things Municipal in a clearer light than they? The S.M.C. despite its numerous promises still withholds from the public all its important doings. What does it pay a Press Liaison Officer for? The criticism in the Press has not been directed at individual efficiency but at the whole Municipal employment organization which very many of the public state quite openly has not moved with the times. What may be but peccadilloes in good times become intolerable faults in times such as we are passing through.
If we could only adjust our present outlook to what is in store for us instead of yearning for the return of the gold rush fever that affected Shanghai during, and for some number of years, after the Great War, ending somewhere round 1932, accepting with good grace the departure from the money-madness which possessed so many of us (including our City Fathers) into normalcy, I for one think that confidence would be more quickly restored to this city. And the S.M.C. should show the way by refusing to countenance the wastage of public funds that goes on under the supposed plea of necessity. In the hey-day of things, when champagne flowed freely and quite stupidly in our night-haunts, the S.M.C. also threw discretion to the winds and created posts for which there was no call. The confidence of the public cannot but have been shaken however slightly by such goings-on and if the complaints directed against the Council in your columns have been somewhat coloured with extremist views the Council has only itself to blame. The "nepotism" connected with certain appointments even of recent date must be answered for.
I have had occasion lately to speak to several highly paid employees of the Council who freely admitted their agreement with the view that an all-round reduction in Salaries and/or allowances (after careful examination of the case of each class of employee) would not be a hardship and would be quite in keeping with the situation as it is. They too could not see why the interests of only a few were sacrificed upon the altar of economy when those best able to face a "cut" were left severely alone. I accuse your contributor of being deliberately misleading for leaving this aspect of the question out of his article. In fact my criticism of the S.M.C. was based practically on this contention. I will not however suggest that he is unfair, preferring to give him the benefit of the doubt.
Neither he nor any of the public need worry as to the Municipal employee being unable to look after himself. Sleepless nights need not be our lot on that count. As a body, the Municipal employee can shout as lustily as any new-born babe where his interests are affected and if he has not to go through the press it is because he has directly the ear of the S.M.C. in whose maternal care he need not fear very much for the future. To suggest therefore that he is being unfairly attacked as your contributor appears to make out is farcical and deceives nobody.
P. H. PREVOT.
Shanghai, June 4.

支持调查
致《字林西报》编辑

先生，——贵报6月3日刊载的投稿人关于工部局薪金等的文章大有可取之处，因为他实际上倡导了我所主张的观点，即根据变化的情况进行修订。这种修订最好通过建立一个完全独立的委员会来实现，该委员会由与工部局没有任何关联的人士组成，且这些人未必是商人。我强调“独立”一词。

您的投稿人反对盲目批评，并暗示有人对市政服务人员进行了诽谤，而这些人根据游戏规则无法反击。我否认曾对担任市政职务的个人进行过任何诽谤，并挑战作者证明其说法。他为何认为批评者比他更盲目？他拥有何种品质或属性，使他能比批评者更清晰地看待市政事务？尽管工部局做出了诸多承诺，但仍向公众隐瞒其所有重要行动。它支付新闻联络官薪水是为了什么？新闻界的批评并非针对个人效率，而是针对整个市政雇佣组织，许多公众公开表示该组织未能与时俱进。在好时光里可能只是小过错的事情，在我们正经历的这样的时代变成了不可容忍的缺陷。

如果我们能调整目前的眼光以适应未来的情况，而不是渴望回归大战期间及之后数年（大约结束于1932年左右）影响上海的淘金热狂热，优雅地接受从支配我们许多人（包括我们的城市父老）的金钱疯狂中回归常态，我个人认为这样能更快地恢复对本市的信心。工部局应以身作则，拒绝纵容在所谓必要借口下进行的公共资金浪费。在鼎盛时期，当香槟在我们的夜生活场所自由且愚蠢地流淌时，工部局也抛却了审慎，设立了并无需求的职位。公众的信心不可避免地会受到此类行为的影响，哪怕只是轻微动摇，如果贵报栏目中针对委员会的投诉带有一些极端主义观点的色彩，委员会只能怪自己。即使是近期某些任命中的“任人唯亲”现象也必须得到解释。

最近我有机会与几位工部局的高薪雇员交谈，他们 freely 承认同意这一观点，即在对每类雇员的情况进行仔细审查后，全面降低薪金和/或津贴并不会造成困难，且完全符合当前局势。他们也看不出为什么只有少数人的利益被牺牲在节约的祭坛上，而那些最有能力承受“减薪”的人却被完全放过。我指责您的投稿人故意误导，因为在文章中遗漏了这一方面的问题。事实上，我对工部局的批评几乎就是基于这一论点。不过，我不会暗示他不公平，宁愿给予他疑点利益。

他和公众都无需担心市政雇员无法照顾自己。在这方面，我们不必失眠。作为一个群体，市政雇员在利益受到影响时，能像任何新生儿一样大声呼喊，如果他不需要通过媒体发声，那是因为他直接拥有工部局的倾听，在其母性关怀下，他无需过多担心未来。因此，暗示他受到不公平攻击，正如您的投稿人似乎所表述的那样，是滑稽的，骗不了任何人。

P. H. 普雷沃（PREVOT）
上海，6月4日。

MUNICIPAL SALARIES
Effect of Depression

To the Editor of the
"NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS"

SIR,—It is evident from ANGLO-LATIN's letter of the 27th inst. that there is an absence of bones in Shanghai. It is good to hear at the same time that the box-makers along Broadway are prospering. I was wondering why, when it occurred to me that the possible reason lay in the fact that they have probably been making boxes to hold the bones in, otherwise where could these bones have gone?
I hope that we can all admire, too, your correspondents' brand of economics which is quite in keeping with what is bringing on ruination to the world and to Shanghai. He seems to find it quite natural that the box-makers as a body succeed at the expense of some other commercial or trading body. It is like rejoicing at a dog which, beginning by swallowing its own tail, keeps the process up till there is nothing left to chew. May I request that he and others interested be good enough to read "Breakdown" by Robert Briffault. He and they will see clearly why there is little hope for recovery until we recognize the axiom that the greatest good we can do to ourselves is to help others and not profit by their misery.
The best answer any enquirer can have to the question why there is such deep feeling in general against the Council's employment policy may be found on page 10 of your issue of the 28th under the title "Fire Brigade Staff Reductions." Each individual may have his own opinion as to whether Council pay (plus all the various allowances already detailed in correspondence) especially for the higher-ups, is excessive or not. That
（手写签名）
is only the financial or narrow view. There is a much broader view to take of this whole question of economy and that is to my mind the one that derives from the social outlook. And if the Ratepayers fight their battle on such a ground they must willy-nilly win out. Comparisons of commercial salaries with the Municipal, or of S.M.C. emoluments with those of the London County Council are, as I said, not always fair, as considerations of country, service, experience, etc. come into play which would prolong argument to a practically negative result. But no contention however brilliant can possibly justify the visiting of the "small" man with the terrible social disease of unemployment when others who get $3,000 to $3,500 a month are not even asked to contribute their share. This is the sort of thing that makes for revolutions. ANGLO-LATIN calls them "explosions." But some will say (referring to any one of the higher-ups in the Council's employ) "A man of his intellect and experience should get $3,000 to $3,500 a month (plus allowances!)" I will retort that there are without doubt thousands of men of far greater intellect and experience who are to-day glad to get the gift of a daily crust of bread and a cup of coffee, let alone all the luxuries that go with the salaries above-mentioned. So you see that the argument cannot hold. If the Council wishes to put my statement to the test it can easily do so by advertising for men of the "intellect and experience" required at lower salaries than those at present paid and see the result. The way some have of comparing $16 to £1 or G.$5 in the matter of salaries is utter nonsense and deceives nobody, as $16 locally, standard for standard of necessary living expenses, purchase much more than £1 in England or G.$5 in the U.S.A.
I could go on with argument after argument on this subject but it is not only with one's hand on one's purse that the matter must be treated. Living expenses, rents, clothing, etc. have come down here and everywhere. Non-necessaries are left out of more budgets. However, lower prices are absolutely necessary all round if we are to successfully combat the stranglehold finance has on us to-day. Interest rates in most countries have been drastically reduced. Municipal Income here is coming down in conjunction with the lowering of rents and the numerous vacancies that are occurring in nearly all landed estates. Is it fair or unfair that the Municipal employee should refrain from doing his part? When commercial salaries were high here, he raised an outcry to have his own emolument "brought up to scratch." Does he think it really unjust that with the all-round reductions that have taken place he should be asked by the public, whose servant he is, to do his little bit?
The fact that 153 unnecessary employees were carried on the books of the Fire Department is rather an indication of something being drastically wrong with the way employments have been doled out in the S.M.C. There is also the little matter of the totally unnecessary posts which are still being upheld at extremely high cost to the Ratepayer without benefit whatever to the City. I will not mention them again to avoid appearing personal, but they are known to all and sundry. My views on the value for cost of the S.V.C. are public property. Social Services lack funds.

P. H. PARVOR.
Shanghai, May 20.

市政薪金
经济萧条的影响

致《字林西报》编辑先生：

先生，——从“盎格鲁-拉丁人”（ANGLO-LATIN）本月27日的来信中可以明显看出，上海已无“骨气”可言。与此同时，听说百老汇路（Broadway）沿线的制箱商生意兴隆，这倒是件好事。我起初纳闷这是为什么，后来想到，可能的原因在于他们大概一直在制作用来装这些“骨头”的箱子，否则这些骨头能去哪儿呢？
我希望我们也能欣赏一下贵报通讯员的那套经济学说，这与正给世界和上海带来毁灭的因素完全吻合。他似乎认为，制箱商作为一个群体以牺牲其他商业或贸易群体为代价而取得成功，是再自然不过的事。这就像是为一只狗欢呼，它从吞食自己的尾巴开始，一直持续这个过程，直到没有什么可嚼为止。可否请他和所有感兴趣的人读一读罗伯特·布里福（Robert Briffault）的《崩溃》（Breakdown）一书。他和他们将会清楚地看到，除非我们认识到这样一个公理——即我们能给予自己的最大善行是帮助他人，而非从他人的苦难中牟利——否则复苏的希望渺茫。
对于为何普遍对工部局的用人政策怀有如此强烈的不满情绪这一问题，任何询问者所能得到的最佳答案，可见于贵报28日刊第10页题为“消防队人员裁减”的文章中。每个人对于工部局的薪酬（加上信函中已详述的各种津贴），尤其是高层人员的薪酬是否过高，可能各有看法。那
（手写签名）
仅仅是财务上或狭隘的观点。对于整个节约问题，还有一个更广阔的视角，在我看来，那就是源于社会观的视角。如果纳税人以此为基础进行斗争，他们必将获胜。将商业薪金与市政薪金进行比较，或将上海工部局（S.M.C.）的薪酬与伦敦郡议会（London County Council）的薪酬进行比较，正如我所说，并不总是公平的，因为国家、服务性质、经验等因素都会起作用，这将使争论延长，却几乎得不出任何结果。但是，无论多么精彩的辩驳，都不可能为让“小人物”遭受失业这一可怕的社会弊病而开脱，尤其是当那些月薪高达3,000至3,500美元的人甚至未被要求分担其责任时。这正是引发革命的那种事情。“盎格鲁-拉丁人”称其为“爆发”。但有人会说（指工部局雇员中的任何一位高层人士）：“像他这样才智和经验的人，理应获得每月3,000至3,500美元（外加津贴！）”我会反驳说，毫无疑问，如今有成千上万才智和经验远胜于他的人，只要能每天得到一块面包和一杯咖啡就心满意足了，更不用说上述高薪所伴随的所有奢侈品了。所以你看，这种论点是站不住脚的。如果工部局想验证我的说法，它可以轻易地通过刊登广告，以低于目前支付的薪金招募具备所需“才智和经验”的人员，并观察结果。有些人将16美元比作1英镑或5金元（G.$5）来讨论薪金问题，这纯属胡扯，骗不了任何人，因为就必要生活费用的标准而言，本地的16美元比英国的1英镑或美国的5金元能购买到更多的东西。
我可以就这个问题继续提出一个又一个论点，但对待此事不能只盯着钱包。这里以及各地的生活费、租金、服装费等都已下降。许多预算中已剔除了非必需品。然而，如果我们要成功应对当今金融对我们的扼制，全面降低价格是绝对必要的。大多数国家的利率已大幅下调。随着租金降低以及几乎所有房地产出现的大量空置，这里的市政收入也在下降。市政雇员 refrain from doing his part（原文此处语义稍显模糊，结合上下文意为“不尽本分/不做出贡献”）是否公平？当这里的商业薪金高涨时，他大声疾呼要求将自己的薪酬“提高到相应水平”。难道他认为，在全面降薪已经发生的情况下，作为公众仆人的他被公众要求尽一点微薄之力，真的是不公平的吗？
消防部门名册上列有153名冗余员工，这一事实相当表明上海工部局（S.M.C.）在分配就业岗位的方式上存在严重问题。还有一些完全不必要的职位，仍以极高的成本由纳税人维持，对城市毫无益处。为避免显得针对个人，我不再提及它们，但这些职位众所周知。我对上海义勇队（S.V.C.）性价比的看法已是公开信息。社会服务缺乏资金。

P. H. PARVOR.
上海，5月20日。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, TUESDAY, MAY 26, 1936

S. V. C.
Value of Figures

To the Editor of the
"NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS"

SIR,—I certainly cannot agree with Mr. BRUCE LOCKHART's contention that "an informed and intelligent public opinion can scarcely be expected to emerge from a maze of public discussion etc." He is referring to the discussion about the S.V.C.

I am afraid that Mr. Lockhart does not see the forest for the trees and knowing him as I do I can justly say that he is sadly bitten by what I shall call the "Statistics bug." If it is his intention of showing the public the rise in the costs of the Volunteer Corps, let him say so clearly, otherwise there is little point in the "maze" of figures which he trots out for our edification. We all know those figures have appeared in the Municipal Reports. It is difficult enough to hold public interest in matters of the present—wherefore this raking up of the past. Whatever was spent between 1929 and 1935—or for that matter, between 1841 and 1935—is gone and paid for and mourning over the passage will do us no good. Taking as example the practically white elephant the Central Administrative Building represents, it would be easy to go on prattling over the past sins of the S.M.C. But would such a course serve any immediate purpose?

An object may be costly at half-a-million in this year of grace and cheap at twice the figure the year before, or vice-versa. That is a matter of circumstance. Where an expenditure of $10,000,000 would be sanctioned gladly on the grounds of necessity, a demand for $10 would be vetoed for a contrary cause. Mr. BRUCE LOCKHART is confounding costs with value and though your readers may have reason to thank him for his self-imposed task (which was not as difficult as you try to make out Bruce, was it now?) I really do not see that he has materially helped in moulding public opinion. The last published cost of the S.V.C. is $720,000. I have argued that—and so far I have not seen any refutation of the points I raised—the sum represents what will be in value a complete waste if maintained. I may be wrong but I know from what I have heard and what has been addressed to me that my views have excellent support. Opinion has been stirred far more than Mr. LOCKHART seems to think. He must remember that most people are thoroughly diffident about "coming out into the open" with their ideas. I know from experience how heavy at times the punishment can be and how unjust and I can therefore well understand such an attitude.

P. H. PREVOT.
Shanghai, May 25.

上海义勇队（S. V. C.）
数据的价值

致《字林西报》编辑先生：

先生，——我确实无法同意布鲁斯·洛克哈特（BRUCE LOCKHART）先生的观点，即“很难指望从一团乱麻般的公共讨论等之中产生出知情且明智的公众舆论”。他所指的是关于上海义勇队（S.V.C.）的讨论。

恐怕洛克哈特先生只见树木不见森林，鉴于我对他的了解，我可以公正地说，他深受我称之为“统计癖”的困扰。如果他的意图是向公众展示义勇队成本的上升，让他清楚地说出来，否则他为了启发我们而罗列出的那团“数据迷宫”就没有什么意义。我们都知道这些数据曾出现在市政报告中。要维持公众对当前事务的兴趣已经够难的了——何必去翻旧账。1929年至1935年间——或者就此而言，1841年至1935年间——花费的任何款项都已支付完毕，为过去哀叹对我们没有任何好处。以中央行政大楼这个几乎成为累赘的例子来说，喋喋不休地谈论上海工部局（S.M.C.）过去的罪过很容易。但这样做有什么 immediate purpose（即时目的）吗？

在今年，某物可能以五十万的价格显得昂贵，而在去年以两倍的价格却显得便宜，反之亦然。这是一个环境情境的问题。出于必要理由，人们会欣然批准1,000万美元的支出；而出于相反的原因，10美元的请求也会被否决。布鲁斯·洛克哈特先生混淆了成本与价值，虽然读者们可能有理由感谢他自告奋勇承担的任务（这并不像你试图描述的那样困难，对吧，布鲁斯？），但我真的看不出他在塑造公众舆论方面提供了实质性的帮助。上海义勇队（S.V.C.）最近公布的成本为720,000美元。我曾论证过——至今我未看到对我提出的观点有任何反驳——如果维持现状，这笔金额在价值上将完全是浪费。我可能是错的，但从我听到的以及寄给我的信件中我知道，我的观点得到了极好的支持。舆论被激起的程度远超洛克哈特先生所想。他必须记住，大多数人对于“公开表达”自己的想法非常谨慎。我从经验中知道，有时惩罚是多么沉重和不公，因此我能充分理解这种态度。

P. H. PREVOT.
上海，5月25日。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, SUNDAY, MAY 17, 1936

VOLUNTEER SPIRIT
Mr. P. H. Prevot Replies

To the Editor of the
"NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS"
SIR,—Mr. Cohen has not quite got out of the maze in which he has involved himself by employing the somewhat insulting term "slacker." A "Volunteer" Corps is one which relies or should rely for its membership upon parties who are understood to have used their own free-will. Why therefore does he have to cast a slur upon the character of any individual, young or old, who chooses to exercise that selfsame free-will according to his particular concepts. By all means recruit if you can, Mr. Cohen, but it is not for you (or anybody) to insult in such a personal way!
And if the S.V.C. is a "volunteer" unit, wherefore the very goodly proportion of paid officers and men?
OLD SHANGHAI RESIDENT asks me to "think of my life." This injection of the element of fear moves some people but I am afraid it has little effect on me. I have thought of my life and the lives of my friends and the thousands around me and I still remain unshaken in my original conviction. But why does he say "We must have both the Police and Volunteer Service, etc."? I am all in favour of the Police, so he cannot have read me correctly. I still contend that the S.V.C. would be every bit as useful turned into a properly drilled Police Unit. From the point of view of economy let me call his attention, and that of those interested, to the following figures of comparison. The force of 520 Specials costs the City about $30,000 annually as against $720,000 paid on account of four times that number of Volunteers. In simpler terms, at an expenditure of say $360,000 the Council could get 6,000 Police. And Police work is constant—Volunteer work eventual and consequently spasmodic.
Might I make one request to my critics; I think they might at least offer reasons for their statements. It would help their cause a lot more.
P. H. PREVOT.
Shanghai, May 16.

***Mr. PREVOT is exceeding the bounds of fairplay. Mr. COHEN has a perfect right to describe as "slackers" able-bodied men who are eligible for recruitment, have leisure at their disposal and do not join the Volunteers. Only those who fit the cap need get out of breath or angry with Mr. COHEN.

志愿精神
P. H. Prevot 先生回复

致《字林西报》编辑先生：
先生，——科恩（Cohen）先生使用“懒汉”（slacker）这个略带侮辱性的词汇，并未完全摆脱他使自己陷入的混乱局面。“义勇”队是一支依靠或应当依靠基于自愿加入的成员组成的队伍。那么，他为何要对任何选择根据其特定观念行使同样自由意志的个人，无论老少，进行人格抹黑呢？科恩先生，如果你能招到人，尽管去招，但你（或任何人）无权进行如此人身攻击式的侮辱！
如果上海义勇队（S.V.C.）是一支“志愿”部队，为何其中有相当比例的是领薪水的军官和士兵？
一位“老上海居民”让我“想想我的性命”。这种注入恐惧因素的做法可能会打动一些人，但恐怕对我影响甚微。我想过我的性命，想过我朋友以及周围成千上万人的性命，但我最初的信念依然坚定不移。但他为何说“我们必须同时拥有警察和义勇服务等”？我完全支持警察，所以他肯定没有正确理解我的意思。我仍然坚持认为，如果将上海义勇队（S.V.C.）转变为一支训练有素的警察部队，其效用将丝毫不减。从节约的角度来看，让我提请他和感兴趣的人士注意以下对比数据。520名特别警察（Specials）每年耗资约30,000美元，而人数为其四倍的义勇队则耗费720,000美元。简而言之，花费360,000美元，工部局就可以雇佣6,000名警察。而且警察工作是常态化的——义勇队的工作则是偶发性的，因而也是间歇性的。
我能否对我的批评者提出一个请求；我认为他们至少应该为自己的陈述提供理由。这对他们的事业会有更大帮助。
P. H. PREVOT.
上海，5月16日。

***普雷沃（PREVOT）先生超出了公平竞争的界限。科恩（COHEN）先生完全有权利将那些符合招募条件、有空闲时间却不加入义勇队的身体健全的男性描述为“懒汉”。只有那些戴这顶帽子合适的人才需要对科恩先生感到气喘吁吁或愤怒。

MUNICIPAL matters
Economy Urged
To the Editor of the
"NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS"
SIR,—I do not intend that the discussions I have raised by a free expression of my views in these columns degenerate into a cheap free-for-all where personal abuse under the guise of public-spiritedness is used as an offensive or defensive weapon.
That is why I am answering your leaderette of this morning. Mr. H. H. Cohen was perfectly justified in calling for greater recruitment in the S.V.C.—since he believes in its usefulness—and of criticizing my contrary belief. But in the use of the term "slacker" he was unfortunately personal and he got what he deserved. And he will get more if he persists in that sort of game. So will anybody, whatever his position in this city, who emulates him. I am discussing the Public Services and their usefulness in relation to cost, not the personal foibles of any individual or individuals.
Now I shall reply to your own comments. May I ask you to accept what I say in the same good spirit as I accept your criticism. Your leaderettes are very weak. Your counter attacks are mere thrusts unbacked by any good reasoning. You omit to take into consideration the matter of change of circumstances when dealing either with Municipal Salaries or the S.V.C. The human touch is completely lacking in your articles and I for one have the impression, rightly or wrongly, that editorial broadmindedness is absent. You say that I "garbled" the purport of your leader on Municipal Salaries. I confess that in many many cases I am compelled in my mind to deal likewise with a number of your editorials. You must pardon my ignorance, but more directness of expression and less jugglery of words and phrases, however well-sounding, would please quite a number of your more assiduous readers.
I respect and welcome every opinion you or your correspondents emit which are intended to contradict my own. But so far let me say that, apart from sentimentality, little if any reasoning has been adduced to strengthen such opinions. Again I must plead ignorance or just plain stupidity.
In the matter of Municipal Salaries the position is clear. By far the greater number of Shanghailanders, foreign and Chinese, have found their incomes and their standards of living dangerously reduced. Municipal economy is a crying need, yet nothing is done in respect of Municipal Servants excepting the scandalous throwing out of employment of a few unfortunates. I rebel at the callousness of the whole business and so do thousands of others. By all means let the Council respect contractual engagements; nothing however can prevent a fair compromise being offered to office-holders. Recalcitrants can easily be dealt with at a later date.
As regards the higher-paid posts, there is not one of them which would not be gladly refilled by the present incumbent at a much more moderate salary. This is not a matter of taking advantage of bad times. It is a matter of sound finance and social fairness. Replacements would not be a difficult affair. Created posts should be abolished.
If the Commission I suggested, and which you approved of, be appointed I trust that it will consist of men known for their thoroughly independent views and social-mindedness. As for the S.V.C., I purposely left myself open to correction. From perusal of your columns no one appears to know exactly what its functions are or are destined to be. To me nevertheless they seem quite clear. Again I am wrong no doubt. My point is that the Corps as a unit has done its work. Its military character adds in no way to its efficiency. Economy is needed and if disbanding is out of the question reducing it to a Police Special Reserve, drilled and disciplined, would in no way impair its standing or real utility. A military force can only be used after proclamation of martial law and I dare to doubt if the S.M.C. as a non-sovereign body has a right to make such a declaration.
All said and done the Ratepayers as a body will be the ones to shape future policies—not the S.M.C. Will they become articulate openly or will they be satisfied to continue in the same old way? The S.M.C. has by no means been all black. It has done magnificent work in the past and is well worthy of every possible praise in that direction. If it has blundered that is only human. But if it refuses to move with the times, then blundering can no longer be condoned and it must be called to order by those who hold the real power.
P. H. PREVOT.
Shanghai, May 14.
***The Shanghai Municipal Council is the elected representative body of the Ratepayers so Mr. Prevot and this journal are in complete agreement on the point.

Volunteer Staff
To the Editor of the
"NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS"
SIR,—Referring to the correspondence and comments on the S.V.C., may I, as a resident, and incidentally a taxpayer, suggest a really definite move in the direction of economy for the careful consideration of the S.M.C. The S.V.C. must be maintained, but is it ever likely to be called upon to the extent it was, from say 1924-1927, during which period it warranted the expenditure?
During these strenuous times, the official headquarters staff consisted of a Colonel and two Sergeant Majors (instructors). Now Sir, does the present or possible future duties of the Corps warrant the retention of a Colonel, Brigade Major, Adviser, Staff Officer and Battalion Adjutant, together with two Sergeant Majors (instructors)?
Ex-SERVICE.
Shanghai, May 12.

工部局事务
呼吁节约
致《字林西报》编辑先生：

先生，——我无意让我在这些专栏中自由表达观点所引发的讨论，堕落为一场廉价的混战，即借公益之名行人身攻击之实，将其作为进攻或防御的武器。

正因如此，我才回复贵报今晨的社论短评。H. H. Cohen 先生完全有理由呼吁增加上海义勇队（S.V.C.）的招募人数——既然他相信其效用——也有理由批评我与之相反的看法。但在使用“懈怠者”（slacker）一词时，他不幸地涉及了人身攻击，他也因此得到了应有的回击。如果他坚持玩这种把戏，他将遭到更多的反击。任何在这座城市里模仿他的人，无论地位如何，也将面临同样的后果。我所讨论的是公共服务及其相对于成本的效用，而非任何个人或某些人的个人怪癖。

现在我将回复您本人的评论。能否请您以我接受您批评时的同样善意，来接受我的言论？您的社论短评非常薄弱。您的反击仅仅是缺乏任何良好推理支撑的空洞指责。在处理工部局薪金或上海义勇队问题时，您忽略了情况变化这一因素。您的文章完全缺乏人情味，而我个人有一种印象，无论对错，那就是缺乏编辑上的开明态度。您说我“歪曲”了您关于工部局薪金社论的主旨。我承认，在许多情况下，我在思想上也不得不同样处理您的许多社论。请原谅我的无知，但更直接的表达，以及更少玩弄辞藻——无论听起来多么悦耳——会使您那些更为勤勉的读者中的相当一部分人感到满意。

我尊重并欢迎您或您的通讯员发表的旨在反驳我的每一种意见。但到目前为止，我要说的是，除了感伤主义之外，几乎没有任何推理被引用来加强这些意见。我必须再次辩称这是由于无知或仅仅是单纯的愚蠢。

在工部局薪金问题上，局势是清楚的。绝大多数上海外侨和华人居民发现他们的收入和生活水平危险地降低了。工部局节约开支已是当务之急，然而除了可耻地解雇少数不幸者外，在工部局雇员方面未采取任何措施。我对整个事件的冷漠感到愤慨，成千上万的其他人也是如此。务必让工部局尊重契约义务；但这并不妨碍向在职人员提出公平的妥协方案。顽固分子可以在日后轻易处理。

至于高薪职位，没有哪一个现任者不愿意以低得多的薪水继续留任。这不是利用艰难时局占便宜的问题。这是稳健财政和社会公平的问题。替换人员并非难事。应撤销那些因人设事的职位。

如果我建议的、且得到您认可的委员会得以任命，我相信它将由以观点彻底独立和具有社会责任感而闻名的人士组成。至于上海义勇队，我故意留出余地以便纠正。从阅读贵报专栏来看，似乎没有人确切知道其职能是什么或注定是什么。但在我看来，它们似乎相当清楚。当然，我无疑又错了。我的观点是，该队作为一个整体已经完成了其工作。其军事性质并未增加其效率。需要节约，如果解散不可行，将其缩减为一支经过训练和纪律严明的警察特别后备队，绝不会损害其地位或实际效用。军事力量只有在宣布戒严后才能使用，我敢于怀疑工部局作为一个非主权机构是否有权作出此类声明。

归根结底，纳税人作为一个整体将是塑造未来政策的人——而不是工部局。他们会公开表达意见，还是满足于沿袭旧制？工部局绝非一无是处。它在过去做出了卓越的工作，在这方面值得一切可能的赞扬。如果它犯了错误，那只是人之常情。但如果它拒绝与时俱进，那么错误就不再能被宽恕，必须由掌握实权的人对其加以整顿。

P. H. PREVOT.
上海，5月14日。
***工部局是纳税人的选举代表机构，因此 Prevot 先生和本报在这一点上完全一致。

志愿人员
致《字林西报》编辑先生：

先生，——提及关于上海义勇队（S.V.C.）的通信和评论，我作为一名居民，顺便也是一名纳税人，谨建议采取一项真正明确的节约措施，供工部局仔细考虑。必须维持上海义勇队，但它是否有可能像1924-1927年期间那样被大规模征召，而在那段时期其开支是合理的？

在这些艰难时期，官方总部 staff 由一名上校和两名军士长（教官）组成。那么，先生，该队目前或未来可能的职责是否证明有必要保留一名上校、旅参谋长、顾问、参谋官和营副官，以及两名军士长（教官）？

退役军人
上海，5月12日。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, SATURDAY, MAY 9, 1936

MUNICIPAL SALARIES
Mr. Prevot's Views

To the Editor of the
"NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS"
SIR,—The Leader on "Municipal Salaries" in this morning's issue of your esteemed paper savours more of an apologia than a convincing defence of the matter treated. So far as I am concerned it does not really matter whether Mr. Higher-up in the Council is paid $40,000 or $100,000 a year, or whether or not his job has resulted from what some critics term nepotism. So long as the Ratepayers found the system satisfactory and voted the expense and nobody was hurt in the process, there was little to seriously growl about.
But the first growl happens to come from the Council itself. It recognizes the need for contraction of expenditure to meet the ever-lessening income and decides to embark upon a scheme of retrenchment. True to tradition the "little man" is being made to take the whole brunt of all this. He needs every cent he receives in order to so much as exist, but in spite of this, he is being thrown out in large numbers and left to fend for himself in a city where unemployment is rife. With nothing put aside (he has had no time) and nothing to look forward to, his position is indeed a desperate one. Yet are there men in the Council's employ living, as I say, on the very fat of the land or occupying "soft" or "created" jobs—positions that I repeat, can quite easily be dispensed with without in any way interfering with the good work of administration. Why have these men not been asked to make the first sacrifice? They are best able to meet the change.
That is the whole point of my criticism. When into the bargain comes the matter of poverty of social service then the whole position becomes infinitely worse. And yet the Chairman speaks glibly of an increase in the Rates. If he gets his hope fulfilled, little hope is there left for Shanghai's future.
Whilst on the subject, may I point out that your comparison of the local rates and taxes with those paid by Birmingham, Liverpool, Manchester and most American cities, is quite unjustified, as the conditions obtaining in each case are different. You cannot have allowed sufficiently for the differences in the economic scale. That my very-great-grandparent gnawed raw meat off the bone and donned only sheep or bearskin hardly justifies my doing the same to-day. Of course I would delight the ladies—those keen worshippers of cave-man stuff—but I should be immediately ostracised by the male or weaker sex and relegated to the ranks of the cannibal and probably shot on sight. What therefore may be good for Birmingham, etc. etc. need not be, indeed is not, good for Shanghai.
In the matter of overpayment of salary has it occurred to you that
(1) $30,000 is the equivalent of about £2,000 but the real or purchasing value of the money in Shanghai is nearer £4,600. In Slocum-on-Marsh I should venture to say that salary would be a very moderate one!!!
(2) Payment of an over high salary in order to assure integrity of the incumbent is a serious reflection on the moral character of said incumbent? What a commentary on our materialistic civilization!

I do not suppose that much change will happen immediately from all these writings and discussions. The game of patting each other's backs by those who hold the reins of power will probably go on. Sincere and justified criticism will continue to be received with offence or disdain. And all the time the lowly-placed will have to find happiness in being crushed out of existence. But the day of reckoning cannot be very far off. The exploitation of the many for the sake of the very few must have its repercussion. When the boomerang strikes, the force of the rebound will be even greater than that of the delivery.
Finally, does the new Council dare to appoint immediately a totally independent and fair Commission to examine into the above charges? There are plenty of honest and capable men who could carry out the work to everybody's satisfaction—men who have no particular cronies to favour, no axes to grind and no false god to worship. Really independent souls I mean.
P. H. PREVOT.
Shanghai, May 8.

***In regard to Mr. Prevot's two questions it may be stated
(1) The Council's scales of salary are according to the market rates fixed by experience and due regard to the qualifications required and tested by the usual methods of comparison.
(2) It is a fact that the prescription of a scale of salary which ensures to the recipient a modest competence is the best safeguard against corruption.
For the rest Mr. Prevot does not seem to have read the leading article with the care which would have enabled a man of his intelligence to avoid so palpable a garbling of its purport.

《字林西报》，1936年5月9日，星期六

工部局薪金
Prevot 先生的观点

致《字林西报》编辑先生：

先生，——贵报今晨刊登的关于“工部局薪金”的社论，读起来更像是一篇辩解文，而非对所涉事项的令人信服的辩护。就我而言，工部局里的“高层人士”每年领取4万还是10万元薪金，或者他的职位是否源于某些批评家所称的裙带关系，这真的无关紧要。只要纳税人对该制度感到满意并投票批准这笔开支，且在此过程中无人受损，就没有什么值得严重抱怨的。

但第一声抱怨恰恰来自工部局本身。它认识到需要收缩开支以应对日益减少的收入，并决定着手实施一项紧缩计划。遵循传统，“小人物”正被迫承受这一切的全部冲击。他需要每一分收入才能勉强生存，但尽管如此，他仍被大量解雇，任由自己在失业猖獗的城市中自谋生路。由于没有积蓄（他没有时间），也没有盼头，他的处境确实绝望。然而，正如我所说，工部局雇佣的人员中，是否有人过着极其优渥的生活，或占据着“闲职”或“因人设事”的职位——我重申，这些职位完全可以取消，而不会以任何方式干扰良好的行政工作。为什么没有要求这些人做出第一个牺牲？他们最有能力应对这种变化。

这就是我批评的全部要点。此外，再加上社会服务匮乏的问题，整个局势变得无限恶化。然而，主席却轻率地谈论增加捐税。如果他的愿望得以实现，上海的未来就没什么希望了。

借此机会，我要指出，您将本地捐税与伯明翰、利物浦、曼彻斯特和大多数美国城市支付的捐税进行比较，是毫无道理的，因为每种情况下的条件都不同。您没有充分考虑到经济规模的差异。我的曾曾曾祖父啃食生肉、只披羊皮或熊皮，这几乎不能证明我今天也这样做是正当的。当然，我会取悦女士们——那些热衷于原始人风格的热心崇拜者——但我会立即被男性或较弱性别的人排斥，被归入食人族之列，并可能被当场击毙。因此，对伯明翰等地有益的东西，不一定、事实上也对上海无益。

在薪金过高支付的问题上，您是否想到：
(1) 3万元约合2,000英镑，但在上海，这笔钱的实际或购买力价值接近4,600英镑。在斯洛克姆昂马什（Slocum-on-Marsh，音译），我敢说这笔薪水将是非常适度的！！！
(2) 支付过高的薪金以确保任职者的廉洁，这是对所述任职者道德品质的严重质疑？这对我们的物质文明是多么大的讽刺！

我不认为所有这些文字和讨论会立即带来多大变化。那些掌权者互相吹捧的游戏可能会继续下去。真诚且正当的批评将继续遭到冒犯或蔑视。与此同时，地位低下的人不得不在被挤压出生存空间的过程中寻找快乐。但清算之日已不远矣。为了极少数人的利益而剥削多数人，必然会产生反响。当回旋镖击中时，反弹的力量甚至会比投掷的力量更大。

最后，新工部局是否敢于立即任命一个完全独立和公正的委员会来审查上述指控？有很多诚实能干的人可以完成这项工作，令所有人满意——这些人没有特别的亲信要偏袒，没有私利要谋取，也没有虚假的神祇要崇拜。我指的是真正独立的灵魂。

P. H. PREVOT.
上海，5月8日。

***关于 Prevot 先生的两个问题，可以陈述如下：
(1) 工部局的薪金等级是根据经验确定的市场费率，并适当考虑所需资格，通过通常的比较方法进行测试。
(2) 规定一种能确保领取者拥有适度生活能力的薪金等级，确实是防止腐败的最佳保障。
至于其余部分，Prevot 先生似乎没有仔细阅读那篇社论，否则以他的才智，本可以避免如此明显地歪曲其主旨。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, TUESDAY, MAY 5, 1936
SHANGHAI MUNICIPALITY
S. E. REC.
B. D.

Obstacles to be Met

To the Editor of the
"NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS"

SIR,—It makes one feel good to see a member of the Church so openly attacking the sores that plague this God-ridden and hypocritical city of curs. The Rev. Michael Bruce's sermon is not a novel departure for amongst us have we men like the Rev. Witherspoon and Luccock (and at times the Rev. Newsham) who speak to us in plain unvarnished phrases to tell us our duty to one another whatever our condition or circumstance.

But does it not seem a bit odd that Shanghai has suddenly awakened to the presence of terrible social injustices in our midst? I personally have known of them for the last twenty years and touched upon them in various "letters to the papers." Or is it that a certain light has just dawned giving courage to sally forth and deliver battle to the enemy?

It is by no means too late to commence. But having started on what will be a very wearing road I hope nothing will daunt reformers, not even the frowns of disapproval from the little tin-gods who supposedly or in fact rule us. It will be a pity indeed if so much good-will both clerical and lay, fails to accomplish the task.

But to succeed—though I hate to say it—there must be funds, funds supplied by the public of Shanghai. Without official aid either from the Chinese Government or a rather Godless Municipality the task is hopeless, I am afraid. My concern here is not with the former but with the latter. First, the Shanghai Municipal Council must learn that the money it wastes annually can be put to much better use. To be constructive it must first be explained how the wastage occurs viz: in the payment of ridiculously high salaries to the clique of higher-ups; in the creation of much too ornate public buildings and the poor usage to which high-priced land is put: in the upkeep of a Volunteer Corps which is an anachronism. The dismissal of 153 men foreign and Chinese from the Fire Brigade is a crying scandal, when the higher-ups and others have not even been asked to make any sacrifice. The employment in soft jobs of a number of Regular Officers and Warrant officers who have been seconded (that is who possess other jobs) is totally unwarranted and that the whole game of amateur sabre-rattling is completely out-moded. That there is no call for a Rickshaw Board nor real necessity for a Directorate-General.

It is not right to inveigh against the vested interests. As the world is constituted to-day vested interests must and will continue to have the upper hand. In fact they do make for balance which others lack. The economic system as a system is at fault but its representatives are not always the rapscallions they are painted. Amongst the newly constituted Shanghai Municipal Council is new and young blood quite capable of striking out along an independent path and whose good-will you can and will surely win.

Keen opposition however will come from the die-hard and the perhaps-not (a cross between a camel and an ostrich). But their day thank God is passing. Soon they shall join their fathers in the land of the dodo.

先生，——看到一位教会人士如此公开地抨击这个受上帝诅咒、充满伪善的流氓城市中的弊病，令人感到欣慰。迈克尔·布鲁斯（Michael Bruce）牧师的布道并非新奇之举，因为我们中间已有威瑟斯彭（Witherspoon）和卢科克（Luccock）等牧师（有时还有纽沙姆（Newsham）牧师），他们以朴实无华的语言向我们阐明，无论我们的境况或环境如何，彼此之间应尽的义务。

但是，上海似乎突然觉醒，意识到我们中间存在可怕的社会不公，这难道不有点奇怪吗？就我个人而言，在过去二十年中我一直知晓这些情况，并在各种“致报社的信”中提及过。或者，是否因为某种曙光刚刚出现，赋予了人们勇气去出击并与敌人作战？

现在开始绝不嫌晚。但既然踏上了一条将非常耗费心力的道路，我希望没有任何事物能令改革者气馁，即使是那些 supposedly 或实际上统治我们的“小泥塑神像”所投来的不满目光。如果如此多的 clergy 和 lay 人士的善意未能完成这项任务，那确实是一种遗憾。

但是，要取得成功——尽管我不愿这么说——必须有资金，由上海公众提供的资金。如果没有来自中国政府或一个相当不信神的工部局的官方援助，我担心这项任务将是毫无希望的。我这里关心的不是前者，而是后者。首先，上海工部局必须认识到，它每年浪费的资金可以被用于更好的用途。为了具有建设性，必须首先解释浪费是如何发生的，即：向高层小圈子支付高得荒谬的薪水；建造过于华丽的公共建筑，以及对高价土地的低效利用；维持一支已过时的万国商团（Volunteer Corps）。当高层和其他人甚至未被要求做出任何牺牲时，从消防队解雇153名外籍和华人员工是一桩令人痛心的丑闻。任用一批已借调（即拥有其他职务）的正规警官和委任职警官从事闲职，是完全没有道理的，而且整个业余的武力炫耀游戏已经完全过时。既不需要人力车管理委员会，也没有设立总监局的真正必要。

抨击既得利益者是不对的。鉴于当今世界的构成，既得利益者必须且将继续占据上风。事实上，它们确实带来了其他人所缺乏的平衡。经济体系作为一个体系是有缺陷的，但其代表人物并不总是像被描绘的那样是流氓无赖。在新组成的上海工部局中，有新鲜且年轻的血液，完全有能力走出一条独立的道路，而他们的善意你是能够并且肯定会赢得的。

然而，激烈的反对将来自顽固派和那些或许不是（介于骆驼和鸵鸟之间的生物）的人。但感谢上帝，他们的日子正在过去。很快，他们将加入其父辈的行列，进入渡渡鸟之地。

我怀着最谦卑的精神撰写此文，没有任何愤世嫉俗或傲慢之意。如果情况更有利，我会在本地发出更大的呼声。既然如此，我满足于跟随布鲁斯先生或其他人的领导。愿各教会（这些保守主义的温床），无论其教派如何，更多地参与到确保在上海及其他地方实现社会正义的任务中来。这是

P. H. PREVOT.

的真诚祈祷。

上海，5月5日。
